analysis:
The PR changes only docs/reference/protocol-messages.md. The patch adds a documentation section (head lines 198-215) on WebSocket close codes and reconnect wait: close code 1012 draws a wait from serviceRestartDelayRange without growing the backoff, any other code or no close frame uses the next ExponentialBackoff range, and a stable session resets the backoff. The supplied units are base-text excerpts (lines 326-947) of unchanged surrounding content: ModelInfo memory fields, prefix-cache objects, heartbeat, backend_capacity, telemetry, inference_error, attestation_response, models_replace and related messages. The changed hunk itself is visible only in the patch, so I checked the new text against the base excerpts and the threat model.

No code, key handling, attestation, encryption, authorization or cache behavior changes. The documented reconnect behavior touches TB-002 availability only. The coordinator is trusted and already controls connection lifetime. Close-code reading is a provider-side policy with the reason string ignored, so I see no new untrusted-input channel. A malicious coordinator-side close could only influence reconnect timing, which the coordinator already controls through disconnects. The doc states every reconnect sends a fresh register, which is consistent with the re-attestation and endpoint-resumption assumptions (T-053, TB-011).

The base excerpts have no regression from this PR. The prefix-cache statements (the T-041 no-raw-prefix-on-disk posture, detail restricted to enumerated failure raw values, telemetry not used for routing) are unchanged.

Unverified contract: the implementation in CoordinatorReconnectPolicy.swift and its constants (serviceRestartDelayRange, stableSessionDuration) were not supplied. I cannot confirm that the doc matches the code, for example that the delay range is jittered and bounded. This is a documentation-accuracy question only, with no security conclusion depending on it.
